gitCommit.subject: Derive billing interval from the subscription, not the current price ID
gitCommit.body:
Derive billing interval from the subscription, not the current price ID

Four places asked "is this annual?" by comparing processor_plan against
User.stripe_premium_annual_price_id. Stripe Prices are immutable, so changing a
price means creating a new one and repointing the env var — at which point every
existing subscription's processor_plan is a stale ID and compares false. The
check broke exactly when it mattered: after a price change, for the customers
who had been paying longest.

Observed in production after the $149/$1,188 -> $99/$899 change: an annual
subscription rendered as "Plan Mensual - MX$99 / mes - Termina el 19 de Mayo de
2027". A monthly plan running eighteen months.

PaySubscriptionInterval asks the subscription instead: the interval Stripe
recorded in `object` (verified populated on real rows), falling back to the
billing-period length, where >180 days is annual — monthly periods run 28-31
days and annual ones 365-366, so nothing lands near the threshold. Nothing here
needs touching when prices rotate, and no Stripe API call is involved; a lookup
would land in _user.json.jbuilder, which renders on every login.

The price-ID comparison is gone entirely rather than kept as a last fallback.
It is correct only by coincidence, and real Stripe rows carry both `object` and
the period columns, so it would never fire.

Manually granted subscriptions now report nil instead of "month". They have no
Stripe price, so "monthly" was inventing a billing cycle. Clients already type
this field as nullable and emitted null for users with no subscription, so this
is an existing state rather than a new one.

Two specs asserted the old behaviour and were updated. Added a request-level
guard for an annual subscription sitting on a retired price; reverting the
implementation fails nine specs.

Still wrong on that card: the amount. subscription.membership.price_annual is a
hardcoded "MX$899 / año", so a legacy subscriber sees today's price rather than
the one they pay. Same shape of bug, tracked separately.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
